# Azim Premji Foundation

<!-- Generated by `make client-docs`. Do not edit inside the markers. -->

Researched 2026-09-29 · status **complete**

Azim Premji Foundation is an Indian philanthropic foundation established in 2000/2001 by Azim Premji, funded by his irrevocable personal donations (including majority economic ownership of Wipro Ltd), not by corporate CSR budgets. Confirmed as the correct entity (the education/health/livelihoods philanthropy based in Bengaluru, running Azim Premji University campuses) via its own Foundation Reports (June 2025 and December 2024 editions) and university website — not to be confused with Wipro Ltd's separate CSR arm. The Foundation discloses combined 'total spends' (direct work + grants) for FY2021-22 through FY2024-25, works through Field Institutes, ~940-1,320+ grant partners, and university campuses in Bengaluru and Bhopal (Ranchi under construction), across education, health, livelihoods and other themes (gender justice, disability, urban initiatives, governance, land/water/forest, civil society strengthening, constitutional values).

Website: https://azimpremjifoundation.org

## Identity

- **Endowment source (Wipro ownership)**: 66% of the economic ownership of Wipro Ltd forms part of the Foundation's endowment
  > As a part of the endowment created by these donations, along with other assets, 66 percent of the economic ownership of Wipro Ltd is with the Foundation.
  <sub>Azim Premji University website · https://azimpremjiuniversity.edu.in/azim-premji-foundation · confidence high</sub>
- **Founding and funding source**: Established 18 Feb 2000 by Azim Premji; funded by his irrevocable personal donations, not corporate CSR
  > The Foundation was established on 18 February 2000 by Azim Premji. Since then, he has irrevocably donated a substantial portion of his wealth to create the philanthropic endowment of the Foundation. We work in India.
  <sub>Azim Premji Foundation Report June 2025 · https://azimpremjifoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Azim-Premji-Foundation-Report-June-2025.pdf · confidence high</sub>

## Where the work ran

- **Expansion geographies for partner-based work**: Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha, Northeast India, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
  > We are setting up teams closer to our partners, which enables us to focus on certain geographies in addition to the states where we already have institutional presence. This includes Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha, Northeast India, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
  <sub>Azim Premji Foundation Report June 2025 · https://azimpremjifoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Azim-Premji-Foundation-Report-June-2025.pdf · confidence high</sub>
- **Field Institutes geography**: 59 districts across seven states and one Union Territory (Dec 2024); 59 district institutes with 291 Teacher Learning Centres as of March 2025
  > Our Field Institutes are spread across 59 districts in seven states and one Union Territory, directly engaging 2.85 lakh elementary teachers; 1 lakh Anganwadi workers
  <sub>Azim Premji Foundation Report December 2024 · https://azimpremjiuniversity.edu.in/media/resources/Foundation-Report/Report-Dec-2024-For-web-Jan-11-2025.pdf · confidence high</sub>
- **Health/creche work geography**: 814 operational creches across Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Odisha covering 12,037 children (as of March 2025); was 489 creches across Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha covering 6,700 children as of Sept 2024
  > Number of operational creches spread across Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Odisha: 814. Number of children covered: 12,037
  <sub>Azim Premji Foundation Report June 2025 · https://azimpremjifoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Azim-Premji-Foundation-Report-June-2025.pdf · confidence high</sub>
- **Livelihoods work geography**: Chhattisgarh (43 villages, 3,215 households) and Jharkhand (59 villages, 5,304 households) as of March 2025; livelihoods work started 2022
  > Chhattisgarh 43 villages | 3,215 households; Jharkhand 59 villages | 5,304 households; Work started in 2022
  <sub>Azim Premji Foundation Report June 2025 · https://azimpremjifoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Azim-Premji-Foundation-Report-June-2025.pdf · confidence high</sub>

## Implementing partners

- **Example partner: Eleutheros Christian Society (ECS), Nagaland**: Grantee for 3+ years, healthcare/education/livelihoods/community institutions in 5 districts of eastern Nagaland
  > Eleutheros Christian Society (ECS) is another of our partners... Over the last three years, the Foundation has supported ECS in its work with small and marginal farmers on livelihood enhancement, and with the community on healthcare and strengthening of community institutions.
  <sub>Azim Premji Foundation Report June 2025 · https://azimpremjifoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Azim-Premji-Foundation-Report-June-2025.pdf · confidence high</sub>
- **Example partner: Gramin Vikas Sansthan (GVS), Uttar Pradesh**: Grantee since ~2017, working on gender, governance, child development, livelihoods in 7 districts of eastern UP
  > Gramin Vikas Sansthan (GVS) is one of our partners... Its work has helped more than 1 lakh women and 45,000 girls across 800 gram panchayats. Over the last eight years, the Foundation has supported GVS in its work with adolescent girls on their education, health, safety and career development.
  <sub>Azim Premji Foundation Report June 2025 · https://azimpremjifoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Azim-Premji-Foundation-Report-June-2025.pdf · confidence high</sub>

- **Active grant partners FY2024-25** (FY2024-25): 1,320 partner organisations
  > Over 2,500 members and 1,320 partner organisations working across India. ... Partners active in FY 24-25: 1,320

## Programmes

- **Programme themes for grant partners**: Gender Justice; Disability & Mental Health; Urban Initiatives; Children; Governance; Health & Nutrition; Land, Water, Forest; Strengthening Civil Society; Constitutional Values
  > Some of our 'Themes': Gender Justice; Disability & Mental Health; Urban Initiatives... Children; Governance; Health & Nutrition; Land, Water, Forest; Strengthening Civil Society; Constitutional Values
  <sub>Azim Premji Foundation Report June 2025 · https://azimpremjifoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Azim-Premji-Foundation-Report-June-2025.pdf · confidence high</sub>
- **State-government collaboration programmes**: Child nutrition (Odisha); small/marginal farmer livelihoods (Andhra Pradesh); justice for under-trials (Maharashtra); panchayat effectiveness (Jharkhand); welfare access in urban settlements (Bengaluru)
  > We have also worked with multiple partners and state governments to develop a few specific programmes. Some of these are for: Improvement in child nutrition in a few districts in Odisha; Yield and cost improvements for small and marginal farmers in Andhra Pradesh; Justice for under-trials in Maharashtra; Effectiveness of panchayat functioning in Jharkhand; Access to welfare entitlements and basic services in settlements in Bengaluru
  <sub>Azim Premji Foundation Report June 2025 · https://azimpremjifoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Azim-Premji-Foundation-Report-June-2025.pdf · confidence high</sub>
- **University campuses**: Bengaluru (100 acres, operating since 2010/2011), Bhopal (50 acres, started 2023), Ranchi (150 acres, under construction)
  > Campus size: 100 acres Bengaluru; 50 acres Bhopal; 150 acres (Under construction) Ranchi
  <sub>Azim Premji Foundation Report June 2025 · https://azimpremjifoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Azim-Premji-Foundation-Report-June-2025.pdf · confidence high</sub>
